main_text.l: obligandum sufficientis, tum in aliquam
temeritatis suæ pænam, ut discat in po-
sterum sapere & sobriam vitam agere,
ne id in se temerè admittat ebrius, quod
eum sobrium ringat[?]. Sed si adimpletio
promissi cedat juranti in grave damnum
aut incommodum; ut siquis ebrius ju-
raret fundum unde familiam alit vendit-
urum vili pretio: videtur non obligari.
Ob eam sc. rationem, quòd vix ullum
potest esse certius indicium emotæ fede
ua mentis, quàm cum quis vino faucius
d' se facturum magnificè pollicetur,
quod est cum suo magno malo con-
unctum[?]. Quum ergo animus inter
jurandum non[?] fuit plenè liber; pro-
terea nec erit obligatio plena. Is
itaque fortassis in hoc casu erit rei
non bonæ exitus non pessimus, si utrā-
que pars, jurans sc. & is cui juratur,
iri boni & prudentis arbitrio rem
totam permittat: qui statuat scilicet
ex circumstantiis, quotam partem par[t]
jurantem ejus quod promisit, in e-
rietatis[?] & ex ebrietate temeritatis pœ-
am persolvere.

page.notes: The left edge of the scan is cropped: the first letters of many lines (e.g. "aque", "on bonæ", "otam", "ua mentis", "t jurantem", "rietatis") are only partly visible; the reconstructions shown are not certain. Line 'ringat' (sobrium cingat?) is doubtful. A blot over the word "non" (line 16) makes it hard to read; "non" is a guess. "unctum" at line 15 is partly cut off. The hyphenated "in e-/rietatis" is unclear. Long s has been written as plain s throughout. Printed "Ob" at line 10 may be partly cropped. The text may contain a printing error in "sc." (printed "fc."), copied as sc.
